Since this image (or any other embedded image) is not generated directly from code it needs to be ‘embedded’, this will look like this when you drag and drop an image into a cell:

There is an option for images to be dragged and dropped from an external file browser into the markdown cell in most Jupyter editors. The image is then encoded with Base64 within the cell, and no additional file is needed. The attachment code can then be copied and used in a ‘figure’ syntax (see below). The
only works in the cell which you dragged and dropped the image into.
A basic markdown image can be displayed with
(but no formatting options, so the image must be the right size, and already contain a figure number/label and caption if needed, or text can be added below the image).
Most figures will need a caption. The caption should include attribution if it is taken from an external source (if the copyright allows reproduction!).

Figure formatting to be used if figure numbering and caption is not included in the image file (do not worry that the image does not appear in Github, it will work when Jupyter Book page is created, as will the automatic numbering):

```{figure} attachment:50418e7c-3008-466c-b26e-c9033a28668d.png
---
height: 300px
---
Here is my figure caption!
```
The height parameter should be adjusted as needed. Note that it is also possible to use width instead, BUT not both at the same time.
